desktop.name: As an app on your PC
desktop.say: Press “Install” in the browser's address bar, and it opens in a window of its own.

apps.note: The steps for both are in “{{settings}}” under “{{apps}}”. You can open them any time.
apps.open: Open the app and phone steps

phone.name: From your phone
phone.say: Open the same screen on your phone and answer questions from anywhere. Connecting the phone to your PC takes a one-time setup.

apps.title: Use it as an app, and from your phone

flow.lead: This is not a chat screen. At its center is the list of tasks, and your part is three things: ask, answer questions, and check what was made.

send.name: Send a request
send.say: Write what you want done in the input at the bottom, and send it.

flow.title: Send a request, and AI turns it into a task and works on it

turn.name: Your turn
turn.say: When AI has a question or a report for you, the task moves to “{{section}}”.

work.name: AI works on it
work.say: What you sent leaves the input, and in 10 to 30 seconds it shows up as a task under “{{section}}”. You don't have to watch the screen while you wait.

conversation.name: Conversation with the coordinator
conversation.say: Press the line above the input to open it. This is where you read how the coordinator, the AI that takes your requests, took what you sent.

detail.name: Detail
detail.say: Press a row of the list to open it. This is where you read AI's questions and reports.

input.name: Input
input.say: Requests and answers to questions are both written and sent here.

list.name: List
list.say: Tasks are listed in groups such as “{{running}}” and “{{turn}}”.

parts.title: What is where on the screen

answer.name: Send
answer.say: Nothing is answered until you send it.

choose.name: For a question, pick a choice
choose.say: The choice goes into the input. You can also answer in your own words.

turn.note: When a report arrives, read it and press “{{finish}}” if it is good. The task is not finished until you do. To have something changed, write it in the input and send it.

open.name: Open the row under “{{section}}”
open.say: A question or a report is waiting for you.

turn.title: When it is your turn

pending.long: A new instruction arrived. Waiting for the owner to give a new report estimate.

timeView.axisAbsent: The time view is not saved on this device. It loads when the connection is back.
timeView.help: Scroll sideways to move through time. Zoom with ctrl (⌘) + wheel, a pinch, or two fingers. Double-click the time scale to see everything. Point at a line (tap on a phone) for details. Keys: + − 0 N; press → on a title to read its lines in turn.

decide.label: Pick a mini game idea, then have it built
decide.shows: AI offers ideas; pick one and it builds that game.
decide.words: I'd like one mini game I can play in the browser. Suggest 3 ideas and ask me which to build. Then build the one I pick in about 5 minutes. This is a trial run, so keep the effort light. Please write everything in English.

models.label: Have 3 models build a snake game, then compare
models.shows: Different models build in parallel, then you're asked which to keep.
models.words: Please build a snake game that runs in the browser, 3 times in parallel, each with a different model; if there aren't enough models, vary the effort instead. When they're done, ask me which one to keep. This is a trial run, so keep the settings light and take about 5 minutes. Please write everything in English.

settings.label: Set a working rule and how many agents run at once
settings.shows: A rule joins the project policy, and at most 4 agents run at once.
settings.words: Please add this rule to this project's policy: "When you finish, report what you changed in 3 lines or fewer." Also, set this environment to run at most 4 agents at once. Please write everything in English.

welcome.lead: Choose an example to try it out.
welcome.title: Welcome to alpacawork
